name: Senegal
tagline: Where the Sahel meets the Atlantic
summary: The westernmost point of Africa, with Dakar on its peninsula, Gorée offshore, the Sine-Saloum delta, the Djoudj bird sanctuary and a music tradition that shaped a good deal of what came after.

entries.caption: Where the Sahel Meets the Atlantic
entries.description: Desert to the north, delta to the south, and Dakar on a peninsula between them.
entries.subject: the Atlantic breaking below the cliffs at Dakar

entries.caption: Delta and Dune
entries.description: The Sine-Saloum mangrove delta, the Casamance forest, and Sahel sand in the north.
entries.subject: mangrove channels in the Sine-Saloum delta

entries.caption: Djoudj
entries.description: Three million migrating birds winter in the Djoudj — one of the great bird sites on earth.
entries.subject: pelicans massed on the water at Djoudj

entries.caption: Niokolo-Koba
entries.description: Lion, hippo and Derby eland in the south-east, in a park that is slowly recovering.
entries.subject: a game track through Niokolo-Koba woodland

entries.caption: Fouta Djallon Foothills
entries.description: No high peaks — the ground rises to the Fouta Djallon foothills in the far south-east.
entries.subject: rolling hills in the south-east of Senegal

entries.caption: Dindefelo
entries.description: A hundred metres of water off the Fouta escarpment, near the Guinea border.
entries.subject: the Dindefelo waterfall dropping into forest

entries.caption: The Senegal and the Saloum
entries.description: The Senegal river along the Mauritanian border, and the Saloum spreading into the sea.
entries.subject: a pirogue on the Saloum delta at sunset

entries.caption: The Petite Côte
entries.description: Saly, Somone and Cap Skirring — Atlantic sand from the peninsula down to Casamance.
entries.subject: the long Atlantic beach at Cap Skirring

entries.caption: Casamance
entries.description: Palm and rice country south of the Gambia, greener than the rest and quite different.
entries.subject: rice paddies and palms in Casamance

entries.caption: Surf, Sail, Paddle
entries.description: Dakar's surf breaks, pirogues in the delta, and the Paris-Dakar's original finish line.
entries.subject: surfers at Ngor island off Dakar

entries.caption: Teranga
entries.description: The word means hospitality, and it is the thing the country most wants you to notice.
entries.subject: a family gathering for tea in a Senegalese courtyard

entries.caption: Wolof, Serer and Diola
entries.description: Wolof across the country, Serer in the delta, and the Diola of Casamance.
entries.subject: a Serer village in the Sine-Saloum

entries.caption: Thieboudienne
entries.description: Rice and fish, cooked in one pot, and the national dish by common consent.
entries.subject: thieboudienne served on a shared platter

entries.caption: Dak'Art and the Magal
entries.description: The Dakar art biennale, and the Grand Magal of Touba, which moves millions of people.
entries.subject: crowds gathering at the great mosque of Touba

entries.caption: Glass Painting and Weaving
entries.description: Sous-verre glass painting, and the strip-woven cloth of the Manjak weavers.
entries.subject: a sous-verre glass painting being finished

entries.caption: Gorée
entries.description: The island off Dakar, and the house of slaves that stands on it.
entries.subject: the pink house of slaves on Gorée island

entries.caption: Saint-Louis
entries.description: The old colonial capital on its island in the river mouth, with the Faidherbe bridge.
entries.subject: the colonial waterfront of Saint-Louis at dusk

entries.caption: Dakar
entries.description: The most westerly city in Africa, on a peninsula, with the ocean on three sides.
entries.subject: the Dakar coastline seen from the Corniche

entries.caption: Colonial and Sudano-Sahelian
entries.description: The balconies of Saint-Louis, and the mud-and-timber mosques of the interior.
entries.subject: a Sudano-Sahelian mosque in the Senegalese interior

entries.caption: Ataya and the Market
entries.description: Three glasses of tea, poured from height, and each one stronger than the last.
entries.subject: tea being poured from height at a Dakar stall

entries.caption: Short Flights, Long Beaches
entries.description: Six hours from Europe, and beaches with a shallow warm Atlantic in front of them.
entries.subject: children on the beach at Saly on the Petite Côte

entries.caption: Surf and Sail
entries.description: Dakar's breaks, kite-surfing on the Petite Côte, and pirogue trips through the mangrove.
entries.subject: kitesurfers off the Petite Côte

entries.caption: Delta Lodges
entries.description: Small lodges on the Saloum islands, reached only by boat, with birds outside.
entries.subject: a lodge deck over the water in the Saloum delta

entries.caption: Community Campements
entries.description: The Casamance campements villageois — village-owned, village-run, and thirty years old.
entries.subject: a village-run campement in Casamance

entries.caption: Light on Water
entries.description: Delta light at either end of the day, and pink water at the Lac Rose.
entries.subject: pink water and salt at the Lac Rose near Dakar

entries.caption: Bassari Country
entries.description: The Bassari and Bedik villages of the south-east, up in the hills, and rarely visited.
entries.subject: a Bedik village on a hillside in south-east Senegal

entries.caption: The Easy Door to West Africa
entries.description: Stable, straightforward, six hours from Europe, and the friendliest reputation on the coast.
entries.subject: the Atlantic coast road north of Dakar
